## Definition

Let $I=[a,b]\subset\mathbb R$ with $a<b$, and let $C(I,\mathbb R)$ denote the
real-valued continuous functions on $I$. For $h\in C(I,\mathbb R)$ set
$\|h\|_{\infty,I}:=\sup_{x\in I}|h(x)|$. For $n\in\mathbb N_0$, let
$\mathcal P_n(I)$ be the restrictions to $I$ of real polynomials of degree at
most $n$, including the zero polynomial, and define
$$E_n(f;I):=\inf_{p\in\mathcal P_n(I)}\|f-p\|_{\infty,I}.$$
When $I=[-1,1]$, this agrees with the published definition
[[def-best-uniform-polynomial-approximation-error-and-chebyshev-interpolants]].

These quantities are finite and well-defined. The interval is compact by
[[thm-euclidean-heine-borel-pseudocompactness-and-extreme-values]], so each
continuous difference $f-p$ has a finite maximum absolute value. The
polynomial space contains $0$, hence the set of errors is nonempty and bounded
below by $0$; completeness of $\mathbb R$
([[def-complete-ordered-field]]) supplies its infimum.

## Definition

Let $q\ge1$ be an integer and let $U\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval containing $[0,1]$. A real function $f:U\to\mathbb R$ belongs to the smooth derivative-bound class $\mathcal S^q$ when it is $C^q$ on $U$ in the sense of [[def-continuity-and-derivative-on-real-interval]]. For $0\le r\le q$ define $M_r(f)=\sup_{0\le t\le1}|f^{(r)}(t)|$, with $f^{(0)}=f$. These derivative bounds are finite because the derivatives are continuous on the compact interval. They are bounds on the restriction to $[0,1]$, not a norm on arbitrary extensions to $U$; no claim that this class exhausts $W^{q,\infty}(0,1)$ is part of the definition.

## Definition

For a real parameter $\tau>0$, define the period-one Gaussian gridding kernel by the series

$$\phi_\tau(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}\exp\!\left(-\frac{\pi(x+n)^2}{\tau}\right),\qquad x\in\mathbb R.$$

The series is the formal periodization; [[lem-nufft-gaussian-periodization-converges]] proves that it converges absolutely and locally uniformly, so its value is a continuous one-periodic real function. Its Fourier coefficient at $r\in\mathbb Z$ is denoted $\widehat\phi_\tau(r)=\int_0^1\phi_\tau(x)e^{-2\pi i r x}\,dx$ when this integral is used; [[lem-nufft-gaussian-periodization-fourier-series]] computes it exactly. The kernel is nonnegative and satisfies $\phi_\tau(x+1)=\phi_\tau(x)$.

## Statement

Let $d>0$, $0<a<d$, $h>0$, and let $F$ be holomorphic on the strip $S_d=\{z\in\mathbb C:|\operatorname{Im}z|<d\}$ and continuous on its closed substrip $|\operatorname{Im}z|\le a$. Suppose there are $C,\eta>0$ such that
$$|F(x+iy)|\le C e^{-\eta|x|}\qquad(x\in\mathbb R,\ |y|\le a).$$
Put $I=\int_{\mathbb R}F(x)\,dx$ and $I_\pm=\int_{\mathbb R}|F(x\pm ia)|\,dx$. Then the infinite trapezoid sum converges absolutely and
$$\left|I-h\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}F(kh)\right|\le\frac{I_++I_-}{e^{2\pi a/h}-1}.$$

## Statement

Let $d>0$, $0<a<d$, $h>0$, and let $F$ be holomorphic on the strip $S_d=\{z\in\mathbb C:|\operatorname{Im}z|<d\}$ and continuous on its closed substrip $|\operatorname{Im}z|\le a$. Suppose there are $C,\eta>0$ such that
$$|F(x+iy)|\le C e^{-\eta|x|}\qquad(x\in\mathbb R,\ |y|\le a).$$
Put $I=\int_{\mathbb R}F(x)\,dx$ and $I_\pm=\int_{\mathbb R}|F(x\pm ia)|\,dx$. Then the infinite trapezoid sum converges absolutely and
$$\left|I-h\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}F(kh)\right|\le\frac{I_++I_-}{e^{2\pi a/h}-1}.$$

1.1 Define $K_h(z)=\frac{\pi i}{h}\frac{e^{2\pi iz/h}+1}{e^{2\pi iz/h}-1}$. By [F2] and [F3], its poles are exactly $z=kh$, $k\in\mathbb Z$: if the denominator vanishes, its modulus gives $\operatorname{Im}z=0$, and Euler's formula then gives $2\pi z/h=2j\pi$. At each such point the denominator has derivative $2\pi i/h$ and the numerator is $2$, so $K_h$ has residue $1$. ## Statement

Let $a\ne0$, $h>0$ and $\Delta t>0$, and put $\nu=a\Delta t/h$. Fix a noninteger $\nu$. Consider a finite-stencil, translation-invariant linear one-step scheme
$$U_j^{n+1}=\sum_{\ell=-r}^{r}c_\ell U_{j+\ell}^n$$
with real coefficients that may depend on the fixed $\nu$ but are independent of $h$, $j$ and $n$. Assume the scheme is conservative, is consistent with $u_t+a u_x=0$, and is second-order accurate in the local truncation sense. For these fixed coefficients, second-order consistency requires exact matching of the constant, linear and quadratic Taylor moments for the one-step translation. If the update is monotone in the componentwise order on grid sequences, then these assumptions are inconsistent. Thus at a noninteger Courant number no such linear monotone scheme can be second order.

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $H$ be a real Hilbert space. Let $T:H\to H$
and $T_n:H\to H$ be compact, self-adjoint, nonnegative operators. Assume
$T_nx\to Tx$ in norm for every $x\in H$, $\sup_n\|T_n\|<\infty$, and the
family is sequentially collectively compact: for every strictly increasing
sequence $(n_j)$ and every bounded sequence $(x_j)$, the sequence
$(T_{n_j}x_j)$ has a norm-convergent subsequence. Then:

1. If $\mu_j>0$ are eigenvalues of $T_{n_j}$, $\mu_j\to\mu>0$, then $\mu$
   is an eigenvalue of $T$. Thus no positive spectral limit is spurious.
2. If $\mu>0$ is an isolated eigenvalue of $T$ with multiplicity
   $m=\dim\ker(T-\mu I)$, then for all sufficiently large $n$ the open
   interval $I=(\mu-\delta,\mu+\delta)$, chosen so that
   $\mu-\delta>0$ and $\overline I\cap\sigma(T)=\{\mu\}$, contains exactly
   $m$ eigenvalues of $T_n$, counted with multiplicity. Their distance to
   $\mu$ tends to zero, and the associated eigenspaces converge to
   $\ker(T-\mu I)$ in symmetric $H$-gap.

Here $\sigma(T)$ denotes the spectrum, and the symmetric gap between
finite-dimensional subspaces $E,F$ is
$$\max\left\{\sup_{x\in E,\,\|x\|=1}\operatorname{dist}(x,F),\ \sup_{y\in F,\,\|y\|=1}\operatorname{dist}(y,E)\right\}.$$

3.1 If $\dim E_n\ge m+1$ for infinitely many $n$, select $m+1$ orthonormal eigenvectors $x_{n,1},\ldots,x_{n,m+1}$ in $E_n$. Apply [F4] successively to these finitely many eigenvalue sequences to obtain one subsequence on which all converge in $\overline I$. By step 1.1 every such limit is in $\sigma(T)$, hence equals $\mu$. Sequential collective compactness, applied successively to the finite list of sequences $T_nx_{n,i}$, gives a subsequence on which all these images converge. Their eigenvalues stay bounded away from zero, so all $x_{n,i}$ converge in norm. Their limits remain orthonormal and, by step 1.1, lie in $E$, contradicting $\dim E=m$. Thus $\dim E_n\le m$ for all sufficiently large $n$, and together with step 2.1 the dimension equals $m$. [A1, F1, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $H$ be a real Hilbert space. Let $T:H\to H$
and $T_n:H\to H$ be compact, self-adjoint, nonnegative operators. Assume
$T_nx\to Tx$ in norm for every $x\in H$, $\sup_n\|T_n\|<\infty$, and the
family is sequentially collectively compact: for every strictly increasing
sequence $(n_j)$ and every bounded sequence $(x_j)$, the sequence
$(T_{n_j}x_j)$ has a norm-convergent subsequence. Then:

1. If $\mu_j>0$ are eigenvalues of $T_{n_j}$, $\mu_j\to\mu>0$, then $\mu$
   is an eigenvalue of $T$. Thus no positive spectral limit is spurious.
2. If $\mu>0$ is an isolated eigenvalue of $T$ with multiplicity
   $m=\dim\ker(T-\mu I)$, then for all sufficiently large $n$ the open
   interval $I=(\mu-\delta,\mu+\delta)$, chosen so that
   $\mu-\delta>0$ and $\overline I\cap\sigma(T)=\{\mu\}$, contains exactly
   $m$ eigenvalues of $T_n$, counted with multiplicity. Their distance to
   $\mu$ tends to zero, and the associated eigenspaces converge to
   $\ker(T-\mu I)$ in symmetric $H$-gap.

Here $\sigma(T)$ denotes the spectrum, and the symmetric gap between
finite-dimensional subspaces $E,F$ is
$$\max\left\{\sup_{x\in E,\,\|x\|=1}\operatorname{dist}(x,F),\ \sup_{y\in F,\,\|y\|=1}\operatorname{dist}(y,E)\right\}.$$

$\Omega=(-1,1)^2$ have a finite matching affine triangular mesh, and let

## Definition

Let $P(\lambda)=\sum_{j=0}^{m}A_j\lambda^j$ be as in [[def-matrix-polynomial-and-homogeneous-eigenpairs]]. For $m\ge1$, define $mn\times mn$ block matrices $A_c,B_c$ by
$$A_c:=\begin{bmatrix}A_{m-1}&A_{m-2}&\cdots&A_0\\-I_n&0&\cdots&0\\0&-I_n&\ddots&\vdots\\\vdots&\ddots&\ddots&0\\0&\cdots&-I_n&0\end{bmatrix},\qquad B_c:=\begin{bmatrix}-A_m&0&\cdots&0\\0&-I_n&\cdots&0\\\vdots&\ddots&\ddots&\vdots\\0&\cdots&0&-I_n\end{bmatrix}.$$
The **first Frobenius companion pencil** with the sign convention used here is
$$L(\lambda):=A_c-\lambda B_c=\begin{bmatrix}\lambda A_m+A_{m-1}&A_{m-2}&\cdots&A_0\\-I_n&\lambda I_n&\cdots&0\\0&-I_n&\ddots&\vdots\\\vdots&\ddots&\ddots&\lambda I_n\end{bmatrix}.$$
For a vector $x\in\mathbb C^n$ and finite $\lambda$, its **companion lift** is $z(\lambda,x):=(\lambda^{m-1}x,\lambda^{m-2}x,\ldots,\lambda x,x)^T\in\mathbb C^{mn}$; when $m=1$, this is simply $x$.

## Statement

For the $k$th term $e_k$ of the $\operatorname{erf}$ series in
[[def-fresnel-erf-and-hypergeometric-series]],

$$\frac{|e_{k+1}|}{|e_k|} =\frac{|z|^2}{k+1}\frac{2k+1}{2k+3} \le\frac{|z|^2}{k+1}.$$

The displayed quotient is asserted when $e_k\ne0$. At $z=0$, every $e_k=0$, so the series and every tail are zero; the corresponding division-free inequality $|e_{k+1}|\le |z|^2|e_k|/(k+1)$ holds there as well.

Thus, if $|z|^2/(K+2)=q<1$, the tail after terms $0,\ldots,K$ is bounded by
$|e_{K+1}|/(1-q)$. The series converges locally uniformly and equals
$2/\sqrt\pi$ times the integral of $e^{-t^2}$ from $0$ to $z$.

## Statement

For the $k$th term $e_k$ of the $\operatorname{erf}$ series in
[[def-fresnel-erf-and-hypergeometric-series]],

$$\frac{|e_{k+1}|}{|e_k|} =\frac{|z|^2}{k+1}\frac{2k+1}{2k+3} \le\frac{|z|^2}{k+1}.$$

The displayed quotient is asserted when $e_k\ne0$. At $z=0$, every $e_k=0$, so the series and every tail are zero; the corresponding division-free inequality $|e_{k+1}|\le |z|^2|e_k|/(k+1)$ holds there as well.

Thus, if $|z|^2/(K+2)=q<1$, the tail after terms $0,\ldots,K$ is bounded by
$|e_{K+1}|/(1-q)$. The series converges locally uniformly and equals
$2/\sqrt\pi$ times the integral of $e^{-t^2}$ from $0$ to $z$.

1.1 For $z\ne0$, every term in [F1] is nonzero, so dividing successive absolute terms gives the stated ratio. At $z=0$ all terms vanish, and the stated division-free inequality and zero tail follow directly without division. For $k\ge K+1$ it is at most $q<1$, so the tail is dominated by $|e_{K+1}|\sum_{j\ge0}q^j=|e_{K+1}|/(1-q)$. On every disk the ratio is eventually below $1$, proving local uniform convergence. [F1, algebra]

3.1 Let $\gamma:[0,1]\to\mathbb C$ be any piecewise continuously differentiable path with $\gamma(0)=0$ and $\gamma(1)=z$. On a smooth piece, put $\eta_h=\gamma(s+h)-\gamma(s)$. Complex differentiability gives $\operatorname{erf}(\gamma(s)+\eta_h)-\operatorname{erf}(\gamma(s)) =\operatorname{erf}'(\gamma(s))\eta_h+\eta_h\epsilon(\eta_h)$ with $\epsilon(\eta)\to0$ as $\eta\to0$; take $\epsilon(0)=0$. Since $\eta_h/h\to\gamma'(s)$, division by $h$ makes the remainder tend to zero and proves $(\operatorname{erf}\circ\gamma)'(s)=\operatorname{erf}'(\gamma(s))\gamma'(s)$. The derivative is continuous on that compact piece and its real and imaginary parts are integrable by [F4]. Applying [F4] componentwise and adding over the finitely many pieces gives $$\int_{\gamma}\frac{2}{\sqrt\pi}e^{-t^2}\,dt=\operatorname{erf}(z)-\operatorname{erf}(0)=\operatorname{erf}(z).$$ This proves the segment identity and path independence without interchanging a series limit with a line integral. [F4, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

For the terms $c_k$ of $C$ and $s_k$ of $S$ in
[[def-fresnel-erf-and-hypergeometric-series]],

$$\frac{|c_{k+1}|}{|c_k|}\le \frac{\pi^2|z|^4/4}{(2k+1)(2k+2)}, \qquad \frac{|s_{k+1}|}{|s_k|}\le \frac{\pi^2|z|^4/4}{(2k+2)(2k+3)}.$$

Each displayed quotient is asserted only when its denominator is nonzero. At $z=0$, every $c_k=s_k=0$, so both series and every tail are zero. The corresponding division-free inequalities obtained by multiplying by $|c_k|$ or $|s_k|$ hold for every $z$.

omitted term, the absolute tail is bounded by that term divided by $1-q$.

## Definition

For a two-state problem for a flux $f$ on the open state domain $G$ of
[[def-hyperbolic-system-and-characteristic-families]], choose explicit speeds
$S_L<S_R$. A signal speed means the propagation speed of one wave in the
particular Riemann solution being approximated. If the HLL model is used as an
enclosing approximation to that fan, its admissibility hypothesis is that
every such speed lies in $[S_L,S_R]$; this definition supplies no general
wave-speed bound.
Set $f_L=f(u_L)$ and $f_R=f(u_R)$. The HLL flux is
$$\widehat f_{\rm HLL}=\begin{cases}f_L,&0\le S_L,\\\dfrac{S_Rf_L-S_Lf_R+S_LS_R(u_R-u_L)}{S_R-S_L},&S_L<0<S_R,\\f_R,&S_R\le0.\end{cases}$$
In the middle case the model has three constant regions separated by the two
waves $S_L,S_R$ and one intermediate state. The wave-speed enclosure is a
separate hypothesis whenever an approximation claim uses it.

## Definition

For a system as in [[def-hyperbolic-system-and-characteristic-families]], a
discontinuity with constant states $u_L,u_R\in G$ and speed $s\in\mathbb R$ is
a **Rankine–Hugoniot jump** if
$$f(u_R)-f(u_L)=s(u_R-u_L).$$
For a strictly hyperbolic system and $1\le i\le m$, it is a **strict Lax
$i$-shock** if it is a Rankine–Hugoniot jump and
$$\lambda_j(u_L)<s\ (j<i),\qquad \lambda_i(u_R)<s<\lambda_i(u_L),\qquad s<\lambda_j(u_R)\ (j>i).$$

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $V,Q$ be real Hilbert spaces, and let $a:V\times V\to\mathbb R$ and $b:V\times Q\to\mathbb R$ be bounded bilinear forms. If $Q=\{0\}$, the theorem reduces to Lax–Milgram on $V$ with $Z=V$ and $p=0$. Otherwise, if $Q\ne\{0\}$, assume $V\ne\{0\}$. Define $B:V\to Q$ by $(Bv,q)_Q=b(v,q)$ and set $\beta:=\inf_{q\ne0}\sup_{v\ne0}b(v,q)/(\|v\|_V\|q\|_Q)>0$. Suppose $Z:=\ker B$ is closed and $a(z,z)\ge\alpha\|z\|_V^2$ on $Z$, with $\alpha>0$. For every $F\in V'$ and $G\in Q'$, there is a unique $(u,p)\in V\times Q$ satisfying
$$a(u,v)+b(v,p)=F(v),\qquad b(u,q)=G(q),$$
for all $v\in V,q\in Q$. If $M_a=\|a\|$, then one stability bound is
$$\|u\|_V\le\beta^{-1}\|G\|+\alpha^{-1}(\|F\|+M_a\beta^{-1}\|G\|),\qquad \|p\|_Q\le\beta^{-1}(\|F\|+M_a\|u\|_V).$$

## Definition

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

Let $d\ge1$, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded open set, and
let $1<p<\infty$ satisfy $p>\max(1,2d/(d+2))$. Put
$V=W_0^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ with norm
$\|v\|_V=\|\nabla v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}$, $H=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, and
$p'=p/(p-1)$. The Poincaré inequality makes this norm equivalent to the full
$W^{1,p}$ norm. [[lem-pe12-w0p-separable-reflexive]] gives separability and
reflexivity, while [[lem-pe12-w1p-compact-l2-embedding]] gives the dense
continuous compact inclusion $V\Subset H$; these are the hypotheses of the
evolution triple in [[def-pe12-gelfand-triple]]. The compact-inclusion result
uses the stated threshold also when $d=1$, where it reduces to $p>1$.

A measurable flux $a:\Omega\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$ is an admissible
**coercive monotone diffusion flux of p-growth** if it is Carathéodory (for
each $\xi$, $x\mapsto a(x,\xi)$ is measurable, and for almost every $x$,
$\xi\mapsto a(x,\xi)$ is continuous), and there are constants $C<\infty$,
$\alpha>0$, nonnegative functions $g\in L^{p'}(\Omega)$ and
$h\in L^1(\Omega)$, and one
null set outside which, for all $\xi,\eta\in\mathbb R^d$,
$$|a(x,\xi)|\le C\bigl(g(x)+|\xi|^{p-1}\bigr),\qquad a(x,\xi)\cdot\xi\ge\alpha|\xi|^p-h(x),$$
$$\bigl(a(x,\xi)-a(x,\eta)\bigr)\cdot(\xi-\eta)\ge0.$$
The induced operator $A:V\to V^*$ is
$$\langle A(v),w\rangle_{V^*,V} =\int_\Omega a(x,\nabla v(x))\cdot\nabla w(x)\,dx.$$
The growth bound and Hölder's inequality make this pairing finite and give
$\|A(v)\|_{V^*}\le C_1(\|g\|_{p'}+\|v\|_V^{p-1})$ for a constant $C_1$.
The finite-dimensional test-coordinate continuity used in the backward Euler
existence argument follows from the stated Carathéodory and growth conditions
by dominated convergence, as proved in
[[thm-pe12-backward-euler-galerkin-existence-energy]]. No additional global
operator-continuity hypothesis is imposed.

For $f\in L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$, a weak evolution solution is a function
$u\in W_p(0,T;V)\cap L^\infty(0,T;H)$ with a continuous $H$ representative
such that $u'+A(u)=f$ in $L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$ and $u(0)=u_0\in H$.

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be bounded and open, $d\ge1$, let
$1<p<\infty$, and let $0<T<\infty$. Put $V=W_0^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ with gradient norm
$\|v\|_V=\|\nabla v\|_{L^p}$, and suppose $V$ has a continuous inclusion in
a real Hilbert space $H$. If $u_j$ is bounded in $L^p(0,T;V)$ and its image
in $L^p(0,T;H)$ converges strongly to $u$, then a subsequence converges
weakly in $L^p(0,T;V)$ to some $U$, the image of $U$ equals $u$, and
$\nabla u_j\rightharpoonup\nabla U$ in
$L^p((0,T)\times\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$.

1.1 If $\Omega=\varnothing$, the closure definition in [F1] gives $V=\{0\}$, so every $u_j$ and its $H$ image is zero. The assumed strong $L^p(0,T;H)$ limit is therefore $u=0$ even when $H$ is nonzero; taking $U=0$ proves all conclusions. [F1, given, algebra]

1.2 Assume $\Omega\ne\varnothing$, put $Q=(0,T)\times\Omega$, and give $Y_0=(L^p(Q;\mathbb R))^d$ its finite product norm. Each scalar coordinate space is reflexive by [F2]. A bounded sequence in $Y_0$ has bounded coordinates; apply [F3] successively to the $d$ coordinates to obtain one subsequence weakly converging in every coordinate. A bounded functional on $Y_0$ is the sum of its restrictions to the coordinate embeddings, so this is weak convergence in $Y_0$. The reverse implication in [F3] makes $Y_0$ reflexive. The Euclidean-vector norm of $Y=L^p(Q;\mathbb R^d)$ and the $Y_0$ product norm are equivalent because the Euclidean norm and the finite-dimensional $\ell^p$ norm on $\mathbb R^d$ are equivalent. Equivalent norms have the same continuous dual and weak convergence, so $Y$ is reflexive as well. [A1, F2, F3, given]

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Orient each edge coordinate from $0$ at
$\partial_-e$ to $\ell_e$ at $\partial_+e$. For endpoint incidences
$(e,-)$ and $(e,+)$ define the outward derivatives by
$\partial_{\nu_{(e,-)}}u_e=-u'_e(0)$ and
$\partial_{\nu_{(e,+)}}u_e=+u'_e(\ell_e)$. The two incidences are both
included at a loop vertex. For $\iota=(e,\pm)$ write $e(\iota)=e$.
If $u_e\in H^2(0,\ell_e)$, with $H^2$ as defined by
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]],
$v\in V_D$, and each edge has a constant diffusivity $\kappa_e>0$, then

$$\sum_{e\in E}\kappa_e\int_0^{\ell_e}u'_ev'_e\,dx_e =-\sum_{e\in E}\kappa_e\int_0^{\ell_e}u''_ev_e\,dx_e +\sum_{z\in V}v(z)\sum_{\iota\in\mathcal I(z)}\kappa_{e(\iota)}\partial_{\nu_\iota}u_{e(\iota)}(z).$$

Thus zero test traces remove anchored endpoint terms, and a Kirchhoff
condition
$\sum_{\iota\in\mathcal I(z)}\kappa_{e(\iota)}\partial_{\nu_\iota}u_{e(\iota)}(z)=0$ at each free vertex
cancels the remaining terms.

## Statement

For the element of [[def-crouzeix-raviart-local-p1-element]], the face-average
functionals form an isomorphism
$\mathbb P_1(K)\to\mathbb R^{d+1}$. In particular,
$$\frac1{|F_j|}\int_{F_j}\phi_{K,F_i}\,dS=\delta_{ij},\qquad \phi_{K,F_i}=1-d\lambda_i,$$
so every $p\in\mathbb P_1(K)$ has the unique expansion
$p=\sum_{i=0}^d\sigma_{K,F_i}(p)\phi_{K,F_i}$.

1.1 Let $b_j$ be the barycenter of $F_j$. By [F2], the face average of an affine polynomial $p$ on $F_j$ is $p(b_j)$. At $b_j$, the barycentric coordinates of the $d$ vertices of $F_j$ are all $1/d$, while the coordinate opposite $F_j$ is zero. Therefore $\lambda_i(b_j)=0$ if $i=j$ and $\lambda_i(b_j)=1/d$ if $i\ne j$. Hence $(1-d\lambda_i)(b_j)=\delta_{ij}$, which proves the displayed duality identities. [F1, F2, given, algebra]

2.1 The $d+1$ polynomials $\phi_{K,F_i}$ are linearly independent: applying $\sigma_{K,F_j}$ to $\sum_i c_i\phi_{K,F_i}=0$ gives $c_j=0$ by step 1.1. Since $\mathbb P_1(K)$ has dimension $d+1$, they form a basis. Applying the same functionals to $p-\sum_i\sigma_{K,F_i}(p)\phi_{K,F_i}$ gives zero for every face; expansion in this basis then gives zero coefficients. This proves existence and uniqueness of the stated expansion. [step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^3$ be bounded and Lebesgue measurable, let $M:=|D|$, $d_D:=\operatorname{diam}(D)$, $q\in L^\infty(D;\mathbb C)$, and $k\in\mathbb R$. If $M>0$, define $a(x,y)=G_k(x-y)q(y)$ off the diagonal and set it to zero on the diagonal. Then $a\in L^2(D\times D)$ and
$$\|a\|_{L^2(D\times D)}^2\le\frac{\|q\|_\infty^2 M d_D}{4\pi}.$$
If $M=0$, every measurable kernel on $D\times D$ represents the zero product $L^2$ class.

1.1 If $M=0$, then $(D\times D,\lambda_3\times\lambda_3)$ is null and the conclusion follows. Suppose $M>0$. For $x\ne y$, $|e^{ik|x-y|}|=1$ because $k$ is real; therefore $|a(x,y)|^2\le\|q\|_\infty^2(16\pi^2|x-y|^2)^{-1}$ almost everywhere. The diagonal is product-null by F3 and Tonelli, so its assigned value does not alter the class. [given, F3, cases, algebra]

## Example

For $R>0$, let $S_R=\{y\in\mathbb R^3:|y|=R\}$ and take density $\lambda=1$. The classical Newton single-layer potential is
$$S1(x)=\int_{S_R}\frac{1}{4\pi|x-y|}\,dS_y=\begin{cases}R,&|x|\le R,\\ R^2/|x|,&|x|\ge R.\end{cases}$$
It is continuous on $S_R$ with trace $R$. With outward radial normal, the interior and exterior normal derivatives at the sphere are $0$ and $-1$, respectively, so their difference is $1$, the density.

## Statement

On $\mathbb T_{2\pi}$, take the smooth source $\rho(x)=\cos(6x)$ and solve $-\phi''=\rho$ with zero mean. Its exact electric field $E=-\phi'$ is $E(x)=\frac16\sin(6x)$. On the five-node Fourier-collocation grid $x_j=2\pi j/5$, the sampled source is exactly $\cos(x_j)$. The mean-zero collocation solution is $\phi_N(x)=\cos x$, and the computed field is $E_N(x)=\sin x$. At every grid node, $E_N(x_j)=6E(x_j)$. This is a spectral-sampling aliasing example; it is not the centered finite-difference operator defined on the main PIC page.

1.1 Since $6\equiv1\pmod5$, [F2] gives $e^{i6x_j}=e^{ix_j}$ for each $j$. Taking real parts yields $\rho(x_j)=\cos(x_j)$, whose unique odd-grid interpolant is $\cos x$ by [F1]. On the five-mode space $|k|\le2$, the collocation operator $-\partial_x^2$ multiplies mode $k$ by $k^2$, so its only zero mode is the constant. ## Statement

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), as required by the affine-scaling supplier used below.

Let $K$ be a nondegenerate $d$-simplex, $d\ge2$, let $F$ be one of its faces, and let $p\ge0$. For every $v\in\mathbb P_p(K)$,
$$
\|v\|_{L^2(F)}^2\le\frac{(p+1)(p+d)|F|}{d|K|}\|v\|_{L^2(K)}^2.
$$
If $K$ belongs to a shape-regular affine simplex family with $h_K=\operatorname{diam}(K)$ and shape bound $\sigma$, then
$$
\|v\|_{L^2(F)}^2\le C_{d,\sigma}\frac{(p+1)(p+d)}{h_K}\|v\|_{L^2(K)}^2.
$$
For $p\ge1$, the normal derivative of $v$ has degree at most $p-1$ on $K$ and satisfies the same inequalities with $(p+1)(p+d)$ replaced by $p(p+d-1)$. In particular, polynomial normal-flux trace penalties have the explicit scale $p(p+d-1)/h_K$; this is an inverse trace bound, not a p-approximation or a DG coercivity theorem.

## Definition

The **exact augmented RBF finite-difference weight procedure** has the following inputs: a dimension $d\ge1$; an integer polynomial degree $r\ge0$; a finite ordered stencil $Y=(y_1,\ldots,y_N)\subset\mathbb R^d$ of distinct sites that is $(r+1)$-unisolvent for $\Pi_r(\mathbb R^d)$; a real kernel $K$ strictly conditionally positive definite of order $r+1$; an ordered basis $p_1,\ldots,p_J$ of $\Pi_r(\mathbb R^d)$; a center $x\in\mathbb R^d$; a homogeneous constant-coefficient differential functional $L=\sum_{|\alpha|=t}c_\alpha D^\alpha$ with $0\le t\le r$; and a neighborhood of $x$ on which every section $z\mapsto K(z,y_i)$ has continuous derivatives through order $t$. Here $\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^d$, $|\alpha|=\sum_j\alpha_j$, and $D^\alpha$ is the corresponding partial derivative. All arithmetic in this procedure is exact real arithmetic.

If dimensions, distinctness, unisolvence, the kernel condition, or derivative availability fail, return `inadmissible-input`. Otherwise form $P_{ij}=p_j(y_i)$, $b_i=(L_zK(z,y_i))|_{z=x}$, $\ell_j=(Lp_j)(x)$, and
$$M=\begin{bmatrix}K_Y&P\\P^{\mathsf T}&0\end{bmatrix},\qquad g=\begin{bmatrix}b\\ell\end{bmatrix}.$$
Solve $Mz=g$ by exact Gaussian elimination with deterministic partial row pivoting: set $A=M$, $c=g$, and $n=N+J$. For $k=1,\ldots,n$, choose the least $i\ge k$ with $A_{ik}\ne0$; if none exists, return `singular-system`. Swap rows $i$ and $k$ in both $A$ and $c$. For each $j=k+1,\ldots,n$ in increasing order, set $\mu=A_{jk}/A_{kk}$, replace row $j$ by row $j-\mu\,\mathrm{row}_k$ in $A$ and $c$, and set $A_{jk}=0$. After all pivots, solve the resulting upper-triangular system by descending substitution. Return `success` with the first $N$ coordinates $w$ of $z$ and the remaining $J$ polynomial multipliers. The stated strict hypotheses imply that `singular-system` is unreachable, as proved by [[lem-rbf-augmented-system-is-invertible]].

The returned $w$ is an exact mathematical weight vector. The nonsingularity lemma [[lem-rbf-augmented-system-is-invertible]] makes `singular-system` unreachable for every input that passes the stated strict hypotheses. This definition makes no floating-point stability or solver-error claim.

The **exact augmented RBF finite-difference weight procedure** has the following inputs: a dimension $d\ge1$; an integer polynomial degree $r\ge0$; a finite ordered stencil $Y=(y_1,\ldots,y_N)\subset\mathbb R^d$ of distinct sites that is $(r+1)$-unisolvent for $\Pi_r(\mathbb R^d)$; a real kernel $K$ strictly conditionally positive definite of order $r+1$; an ordered basis $p_1,\ldots,p_J$ of $\Pi_r(\mathbb R^d)$; a center $x\in\mathbb R^d$; a homogeneous constant-coefficient differential functional $L=\sum_{|\alpha|=t}c_\alpha D^\alpha$ with $0\le t\le r$; and a neighborhood of $x$ on which every section $z\mapsto K(z,y_i)$ has continuous derivatives through order $t$. Here $\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^d$, $|\alpha|=\sum_j\alpha_j$, and $D^\alpha$ is the corresponding partial derivative. All arithmetic in this procedure is exact real arithmetic.

If dimensions, distinctness, unisolvence, the kernel condition, or derivative availability fail, return `inadmissible-input`. Otherwise form $P_{ij}=p_j(y_i)$, $b_i=(L_zK(z,y_i))|_{z=x}$, $\ell_j=(Lp_j)(x)$, and
$$M=\begin{bmatrix}K_Y&P\\P^{\mathsf T}&0\end{bmatrix},\qquad g=\begin{bmatrix}b\\ell\end{bmatrix}.$$
Solve $Mz=g$ by exact Gaussian elimination with deterministic partial row pivoting: set $A=M$, $c=g$, and $n=N+J$. For $k=1,\ldots,n$, choose the least $i\ge k$ with $A_{ik}\ne0$; if none exists, return `singular-system`. Swap rows $i$ and $k$ in both $A$ and $c$. For each $j=k+1,\ldots,n$ in increasing order, set $\mu=A_{jk}/A_{kk}$, replace row $j$ by row $j-\mu\,\mathrm{row}_k$ in $A$ and $c$, and set $A_{jk}=0$. After all pivots, solve the resulting upper-triangular system by descending substitution. Return `success` with the first $N$ coordinates $w$ of $z$ and the remaining $J$ polynomial multipliers. The stated strict hypotheses imply that `singular-system` is unreachable, as proved by [[lem-rbf-augmented-system-is-invertible]].

The returned $w$ is an exact mathematical weight vector. The nonsingularity lemma [[lem-rbf-augmented-system-is-invertible]] makes `singular-system` unreachable for every input that passes the stated strict hypotheses. This definition makes no floating-point stability or solver-error claim.

## Statement

Let $a=x_0<\cdots<x_m=b$, $m\ge1$, with $h_i=x_{i+1}-x_i$ and
$H=\max_i h_i$. Suppose $f$ has continuous derivatives through order four
on an open interval containing $[a,b]$, and let $M\ge0$ satisfy
$|f^{(4)}(x)|\le M$ there. Let $s$ be the clamped cubic interpolant at
$y_i=f(x_i)$ with the boundary-compatible slopes
$s'(a)=f'(a)$ and $s'(b)=f'(b)$. Then
$$
\|s-f\|_{L^\infty([a,b])}\le\frac{83}{324}MH^4\le MH^4.
$$
The conclusion uses the exact endpoint derivatives; it is not a rate claim
for the natural boundary condition or for estimated endpoint slopes.

## Definition

Input: a finite exact dyadic square matrix $M$ of size $s\ge2$, a selected
floating-point system with known dyadic unit-roundoff bound $u$, and a finite
range certificate listing each exact product or sum in the fixed
left-to-right Leibniz schedule. Verify by exact dyadic comparison that every
entry of $M$ is representable and each listed operation result is either zero
or normal-range. The system must satisfy the standard relative model in
[[def-standard-relative-floating-point-model-and-unit-roundoff]]. Set
$q=s+s!-2$ and $\gamma_q=qu/(1-qu)$; if $qu\ge1$, or if the certificate or
model hypotheses are unavailable, return `inconclusive` without using a
floating result.

1. Enumerate permutations in lexicographic tuple order. Form each signed
   product left-to-right, applying its sign by exact sign change. Initialize the sum
   with the first term; add each later term left-to-right using the selected
   floating-point system. Call the result $\widehat D$.
2. Form the nonnegative Leibniz absolute-term sum using the real absolute
   value [[def-abs-value]] and the outward
   interval operations of
   [[def-outward-rounded-interval-and-ball-operations]] to singleton intervals
   $[|M_{ij}|,|M_{ij}|]$. Its expression DAG is finite; let $U$ be the upper
   endpoint of the resulting finite interval. If any operation is nonfinite,
   return `inconclusive`.
3. Compute $E=\operatorname{ru}(\gamma_q U)$ by the directed rounding of
   [[def-dyadic-floating-point-format-and-directed-rounding]]. If this
   overflows, return `inconclusive`.
4. Compare exact dyadic rationals. Return `positive` if $\widehat D-E>0$;
   return `negative` if $\widehat D+E<0$; otherwise return `inconclusive`.

The computation of $U$ uses outward arithmetic, so the exact nonnegative sum
$S$ in [[lem-leibniz-determinant-forward-error-bound]] satisfies $S\le U$
whenever a finite $U$ is returned, by
[[thm-outward-rounded-operations-are-isotone-and-dag-sound]].

## Definition

Input: a finite exact dyadic square matrix $M$ of size $s\ge2$, a selected
floating-point system with known dyadic unit-roundoff bound $u$, and a finite
range certificate listing each exact product or sum in the fixed
left-to-right Leibniz schedule. Verify by exact dyadic comparison that every
entry of $M$ is representable and each listed operation result is either zero
or normal-range. The system must satisfy the standard relative model in
[[def-standard-relative-floating-point-model-and-unit-roundoff]]. Set
$q=s+s!-2$ and $\gamma_q=qu/(1-qu)$; if $qu\ge1$, or if the certificate or
model hypotheses are unavailable, return `inconclusive` without using a
floating result.

1. Enumerate permutations in lexicographic tuple order. Form each signed
   product left-to-right, applying its sign by exact sign change. Initialize the sum
   with the first term; add each later term left-to-right using the selected
   floating-point system. Call the result $\widehat D$.
2. Form the nonnegative Leibniz absolute-term sum using the real absolute
   value [[def-abs-value]] and the outward
   interval operations of
   [[def-outward-rounded-interval-and-ball-operations]] to singleton intervals
   $[|M_{ij}|,|M_{ij}|]$. Its expression DAG is finite; let $U$ be the upper
   endpoint of the resulting finite interval. If any operation is nonfinite,
   return `inconclusive`.
3. Compute $E=\operatorname{ru}(\gamma_q U)$ by the directed rounding of
   [[def-dyadic-floating-point-format-and-directed-rounding]]. If this
   overflows, return `inconclusive`.
4. Compare exact dyadic rationals. Return `positive` if $\widehat D-E>0$;
   return `negative` if $\widehat D+E<0$; otherwise return `inconclusive`.

The computation of $U$ uses outward arithmetic, so the exact nonnegative sum
$S$ in [[lem-leibniz-determinant-forward-error-bound]] satisfies $S\le U$
whenever a finite $U$ is returned, by
[[thm-outward-rounded-operations-are-isotone-and-dag-sound]].

## Definition

This is a finite aggregation-based algebraic multigrid **setup** procedure; it
constructs a hierarchy and does not claim that any cycle converges. All
arithmetic and comparisons below are exact. An admissible input consists of an
integer $n_0\ge1$, a real symmetric positive-definite matrix
$A_0=(a_{ij})\in\mathbb R^{n_0\times n_0}$ whose off-diagonal
entries satisfy $a_{ij}\le0$, a real threshold $0<\theta<1$, a coarse-size
threshold $n_{\min}\ge1$, and a real level cap $L\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}$. A
matrix with these sign and definiteness conditions is the matrix class used
here. The terms
**strength graph**, **aggregate**, **prolongation**, and **Galerkin hierarchy**
are defined by the steps below.

1. Set $\ell=0$, $n_\ell=\dim A_\ell$, and retain $A_\ell$ in the output. If
   $n_\ell\le n_{\min}$, return status `coarse-reached`.
2. If $\ell+1>L$ before the next aggregation attempt, return status
   `level-cap`.
3. On vertices $1,\ldots,n_\ell$, place an undirected edge $\{i,j\}$ for
   $i\ne j$ exactly when $a_{ij}^{(\ell)}<0$ and at least one of
   $$-a_{ij}^{(\ell)}\ge\theta\max_{k\ne i}(-a_{ik}^{(\ell)}),\qquad -a_{ij}^{(\ell)}\ge\theta\max_{k\ne j}(-a_{jk}^{(\ell)})$$
   holds. This finite graph is the strength graph at level $\ell$.
4. Let $U=\{1,\ldots,n_\ell\}$ and start with no aggregates. While $U\ne\varnothing$, let $i$ be the smallest element of $U$, create one aggregate
   $$C_r=\{i\}\cup\bigl(N(i)\cap U\bigr),$$
   where $N(i)$ is its strength-graph neighbour set, then remove every element of $C_r$ from $U$. This produces an ordered family of aggregates.
5. Let $n_{\ell+1}$ be the number of aggregates. If $n_{\ell+1}\ge n_\ell$, return status `coarsening-stalled` with the hierarchy through level $\ell$. Otherwise form the indicator prolongation
   $$(P_\ell)_{ir}=1\text{ if }i\in C_r,\qquad (P_\ell)_{ir}=0\text{ otherwise},$$
   form the Galerkin coarse matrix $A_{\ell+1}=P_\ell^{\mathsf T}A_\ell P_\ell$, append $P_\ell,A_{\ell+1}$, replace $\ell$ by $\ell+1$, and return to step 1.

The result contains all completed matrices and prolongations and exactly one
status: `coarse-reached`, `level-cap`, or `coarsening-stalled`. Reaching any
status is not a convergence or quality certificate.

## Statement

Under the hypotheses of [[def-coefficientwise-weighted-backward-error-for-matrix-polynomial]], put
$$S:=\sum_{j=0}^{m}\omega_j^2|\alpha|^{2j}|\beta|^{2(m-j)}.$$
Then $S>0$, the infimum is attained, and
$$\eta_F(P,[\alpha:\beta],x;\omega)=\frac{\|P_h(\alpha,\beta)x\|_2}{\|x\|_2\sqrt{S}}.$$
At a finite parameter $[\lambda:1]$ this is $\|P(\lambda)x\|_2/(\|x\|_2\sqrt{\sum_j\omega_j^2|\lambda|^{2j}})$; at infinity $[1:0]$ it is $\|A_mx\|_2/(\omega_m\|x\|_2)$. When $\alpha\ne0$, setting $\mu=\beta/\alpha$ rewrites the same formula for $P^{\rm rev}_m(\mu)$ with reversed coefficient weights $\widetilde\omega_k:=\omega_{m-k}$.

## Definition

Inputs are CARE data with $Q=C^*C\succeq0$, $R\succ0$, a supplied stabilizing gain $K_0$, a finite outer budget $N$, and either exact or safeguarded-inexact solve mode. At iteration $j$, put $A_j=A-BK_j$.

In exact mode, use [[alg-bartels-stewart-sylvester-equation]] to solve
$$A_j^*X_j+X_jA_j=-(Q+K_j^*RK_j).$$
If it does not return success, stop with its status. Otherwise set $K_{j+1}=R^{-1}B^*X_j$ and continue, stopping after at most $N$ updates.

In safeguarded-inexact mode, take a proposed Hermitian approximate Lyapunov solution $\widetilde P_j$, define $\widetilde K_j=R^{-1}B^*\widetilde P_j$, and inspect the finite line-search list $\theta_\ell=2^{-\ell}$, $0\le\ell\le L$. For each trial $K_\ell=K_j+\theta_\ell(\widetilde K_j-K_j)$, let $A_\ell=A-BK_\ell$ and obtain outward-verified data: $W_\ell\succ0$, $\mu_\ell>0$ with
$$A_\ell^*W_\ell+W_\ell A_\ell\preceq-\mu_\ell I,$$
an inverse bound $\kappa_\ell\ge\|\mathcal L_{A_\ell}^{-1}\|_{F\to F}$, a residual bound $r_\ell$ for
$$\mathcal L_{A_\ell}(\widetilde P_j)+Q+K_\ell^*RK_\ell,$$
and an outward upper bound $\eta_\ell\ge\lambda_{\max}(\widetilde P_j-X_j)$. Accept the first trial satisfying $\eta_\ell+\kappa_\ell r_\ell\le0$. If none passes, return safeguard-inconclusive without changing $K_j$. The verifier uses the residual-certificate convention of [[def-verified-linear-residual-certificate-data]] and the finite-DAG enclosure guarantee of [[thm-outward-rounded-operations-are-isotone-and-dag-sound]].

After at most $N$ outer updates return the accepted gain sequence, solve residuals, cost-matrix data, and terminal status. An arbitrary approximate Lyapunov solve is never accepted without the separate stability and descent checks above.

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $U$ and $\omega$ be as in [[def-na-star-shaped-bogovskii-integral]]. For $\phi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$ and $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$, use $\widehat g(\xi)=\int e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}g(x)dx$ and define
$$T_{\phi,j}^{\epsilon}f(x)=\int f(y)\int_\epsilon^1\partial_{x_j}\left[\phi\left(y+\frac{x-y}{t}\right)\right]\frac{dt}{t^d}dy.$$
As $\epsilon\downarrow0$ these converge in distributions to $T_{\phi,j}f$. The part with $0<t<1/2$ satisfies
$$\widehat{T^<_{\phi,j}f}(\xi)=2\pi i\xi_j\int_0^{1/2}\widehat\phi(t\xi)\widehat f((1-t)\xi)dt.$$
When $f\in C_c^\infty(U)$, the Bogovskii formula satisfies $\partial_j(\mathcal B_Uf)_k=T_{x_k\omega,j}f-T_{\omega,j}(y_kf)$ distributionally.

3.1 For $\epsilon>0$, let $\mathcal B_U^\epsilon f$ be the defining integral truncated to $t\ge\epsilon$. For fixed $x\ne y$, the kernel integrand is zero for all sufficiently small $t$, because nonzero values require $|x-y|/t=|z-y|\le C_U$. The truncated fields therefore converge pointwise almost everywhere to $\mathcal B_Uf$; their difference is dominated by the compactly supported $L^2$ majorant $\mathcal K_U|f|$ from [F4], which is integrable on its finite-measure support; dominated convergence gives distributional convergence. Rewrite the $k$-th component using $x_k-y_k=t(z_k-y_k)$ from [F2] as the integral of $[z_k\omega(z)-y_k\omega(z)]f(y)$ against $dt/t^d$. Differentiating the truncated fields in $x_j$, then using step 1.1 for the distributional limit, gives $T_{x_k\omega,j}f-T_{\omega,j}(y_kf)$; the minus sign comes from the second term. [A1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1] ∎

## Statement

Fix $\gamma>1$. For $U=(\rho,m,E)\in\mathcal G_\gamma$, let
$e=E-m^2/(2\rho)$, $p=(\gamma-1)e$, $u=m/\rho$, and
$c=\sqrt{\gamma p/\rho}$. If $a\ge |u|+c$, then both split states
$$U_\delta=U+\delta F(U),\qquad \delta\in\{-1/a,1/a\},$$
belong to $\mathcal G_\gamma$, where $F(U)=(m,m^2/\rho+p,u(E+p))$.
More precisely, with $x=1+\delta u$ their density and internal-energy density are
$$\rho_\delta=\rho x,\qquad e_\delta=e x-\frac{\delta^2p^2}{2\rho x}>0.$$

Let $d,\tau>0$, $I_i=[id,(i+1)d)$, $t_n=n\tau$, and $J_n=[t_n,t_{n+1})$. Suppose vector states and shared face fluxes satisfy
$$d(U_i^{n+1}-U_i^n)+\tau(\widehat F_{i+1/2}^n-\widehat F_{i-1/2}^n)=d\tau S_i^n$$
as in [[def-pe05-hydrostatic-hll-scheme]]. For $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R\times(-\infty,T);\mathbb R^2)$ define the space-time cell average
$$\Phi_i^n=\frac1{d\tau}\int_{J_n}\int_{I_i}\varphi(x,t)\,dx\,dt.$$
Choose $N$ such that $\varphi$ vanishes for $t\ge t_{N-1}$. Then
$$\sum_i d\,U_i^0\cdot\Phi_i^0+\sum_{n=1}^{N-1}\sum_i d\,U_i^n\cdot(\Phi_i^n-\Phi_i^{n-1})+\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\sum_i\tau\,\widehat F_{i+1/2}^n\cdot(\Phi_{i+1}^n-\Phi_i^n)+\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\sum_i d\tau\,S_i^n\cdot\Phi_i^n=0.$$
Every sum is finite because the test is compactly supported.

## Statement

Let $b\in C^2(\mathbb R)$, let the uniform cell width be $d>0$, let $x_i$ be the center of cell $i$, and let $0\le h_i^n\le H$ on a fixed compact space-time cylinder. Set $b_i=b(x_i)$, $\delta_{i,+}=(b(x_i+d)-b(x_i))_+$, and $\delta_{i,-}=(b(x_i-d)-b(x_i))_+$. For the source term $S_i^n$ in [[def-pe05-hydrostatic-hll-scheme]],
$$S_i^n=\left(0,\frac{g}{2d}\left((h_i^n-\delta_{i,+})_+^2-(h_i^n-\delta_{i,-})_+^2\right)\right),$$
there is a constant $C$ depending only on the compact interval, $b$, $g$, and $H$ such that
$$\left|S_i^{(2)}+g h_i b'(x_i)\right|\le C d.$$
For time slabs $J_n=[n\tau,(n+1)\tau)$, define the piecewise-constant source reconstruction $\mathcal S_d(x,t)=S_i^n$ on $[x_i-d/2,x_i+d/2)\times J_n$. Consequently, as $d\to0$, if the corresponding piecewise-constant depth reconstructions $h_d$ converge strongly in $L^1_{\rm loc}(\mathbb R\times(0,T))$ to $h$ and are locally uniformly bounded, then $\mathcal S_d\to(0,-ghb')$ strongly in $L^1_{\rm loc}$.

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and a family in [[def-fv-regular-simplicial-companion-family]]. For $1<p<\infty$ and zero boundary face values, put
$$B_{h,p}(v)^p=\sum_K|K||G_Kv|^p+S_{h,p}(v)^p,\qquad S_{h,p}(v)^p=\sum_{K,F}|F|d_{K,F}^{1-p}|\rho_{K,F}(v)|^p,$$
where $G_K,\rho_{K,F}$ have the formulas in [[def-hybrid-mimetic-fv-scheme]]. Then, with constants independent of $h,v$,
$$C^{-1}D_{h,p}(v)\le B_{h,p}(v)\le CD_{h,p}(v),\quad \|E_hv\|_{W^{1,p}}\le CD_{h,p}(v),\quad \|\Pi_hv-E_hv\|_{L^p}\le ChD_{h,p}(v).$$
Here $E_hv\in W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$. If $p>\max(1,2d/(d+2))$ and $\vartheta=1-d\max(1/p-1/2,0)>0$, also
$$\|\Pi_hv-E_hv\|_2\le Ch^\vartheta D_{h,p}(v),\qquad \|\Pi_hv\|_2+\|\Pi_hv\|_p\le CD_{h,p}(v).$$
For $z\in W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$, $D_{h,p}(I_hz)\le C\|\nabla z\|_p$. If the cell points are volume centroids, then for smooth $z$ with compact support in $\Omega$, $G_h I_hz\to\nabla z$ uniformly and $S_{h,p}(I_hz)\le Ch\|D^2z\|_\infty$, where $G_hv|_K=G_Kv$. Finally, for every smooth vector field $\phi$ on a neighborhood of $\overline\Omega$,
$$\left|\int_\Omega G_hv\cdot\phi+\Pi_hv\,\operatorname{div}\phi\right|\le ChD_{h,p}(v)\|\nabla\phi\|_\infty.$$
Consequently bounded $D_{h,p}(v_h)$, strong $L^p$ convergence $\Pi_hv_h\to v$, and weak $L^p$ convergence $G_hv_h\rightharpoonup g$ imply $g=\nabla v$ distributionally. The same statements hold after integration in time with the corresponding $L^p$ bounds.

On $[0,1]^2$, take degree-one tensor Bernstein functions in each coordinate, all four weights equal to one, and control net

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $F:\widehat\Omega\to\Omega$ be an admissible NURBS map and $W$ its continuous denominator, with $W\ge w_->0$ and cellwise $G_W:=\|\nabla W\|_{L^\infty}<\infty$. Let $\widehat u$ and a numerator spline $s\in S_h$ be $C^1$ up to the boundary of each cell in the common refinement of the geometry and analysis knot grids, with matching traces, and put $g:=W\widehat u$. Then the physical rational spline $v_h:=(s/W)\circ F^{-1}$ belongs to $H^1(\Omega)$ and
$$\|u-v_h\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\le C_F C_W\|g-s\|_{H^1(\widehat\Omega)},\qquad C_F:=\sqrt{j_+}\sqrt{1+L^2},\quad C_W:=\frac{2}{w_-}+\frac{G_W}{w_-^2},$$
where $u:=\widehat u\circ F^{-1}$. This result transfers a specified numerator approximation bound; it does not assert a polynomial-degree-independent rate or a general $H^1$ rate for arbitrary knot families.

## Definition

Input $a<b$, $\omega\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, a real phase $g\in C^{r+1}[a,b]$ with $|g'|\ge c>0$, a complex amplitude $p\in C^r[a,b]$, an integer $r\ge1$, and a certified real bound $M\ge\|T_g^rp\|_\infty$. Compute
$$S_r(p)=\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}\frac{(-1)^j}{(i\omega)^{j+1}}\left[\frac{T_g^jp(x)}{g'(x)}e^{i\omega g(x)}\right]_a^b,\qquad \epsilon_r=\frac{(b-a)M}{|\omega|^r}.$$
Return $(S_r(p),\epsilon_r)$. The nonstationary recurrence and the need for the certified derivative bound are specified in [[thm-na-nonstationary-oscillatory-integration-by-parts]]. If exact phase moments are available, they may instead be passed as exact moment data to a Filon rule; this algorithm makes no general closed-form claim for nonlinear phases.

Let $n\ge0$ be an integer, $x\in\mathbb R$, $m\ge1$, and $h=\pi/m$. Put

## Statement

Let $u_0\in\mathrm{BV}_b(\mathbb R)$ with $V=\operatorname{TV}(u_0)$ and
$I=[a_-,a_+]$. Let $(h_m,\tau_m)$ satisfy $h_m,\tau_m\to0$ and the full
invariant-interval CFL bound for the scheme of
[[def-monotone-finite-volume-entropy-scheme]]. Let $W_m$ and $\mathcal U_m$ be
the piecewise-linear and piecewise-constant reconstructions of
[[def-piecewise-linear-fv-time-interpolant]]. Then every subsequence has a
further subsequence for which $W_m$ converges uniformly in time in
$L^1(K)$ on every bounded interval $K\subset\mathbb R$ to a map
$t\mapsto u(t)\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R)$, continuous in local $L^1$,
with $u(0)=u_0$ and $a_-\le u(t)\le a_+$ almost everywhere. On that subsequence
the piecewise-constant reconstructions converge strongly to the same $u$ in
$L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R\times(0,T))$.
**Given:** $u_0\in\mathrm{BV}_b(\mathbb R)$, the monotone flux scheme, meshes $h_m,\tau_m\to0$ satisfying its full CFL bound, the time interpolants $W_m$, and a finite time interval $[0,T]$.

1.1 For every $t$, $W_m(\cdot,t)$ is piecewise constant with values in $I$ and spatial variation at most $V$: on each time slab it is a convex combination of two states whose variations are at most $V$ by [F2]. Here the variation of a piecewise-constant section on an interval is the sum of the absolute jump sizes inside that interval. Fix an integer $R\ge1$ and consider any sequence $v_m$ of such sections on $[-R,R]$. At each rational point in $[-R,R]$, the values lie in the compact interval $I$. The bounded-value subsequence at one rational point exists by [F6]; explicitly, partition $I$ into finitely many closed intervals of length at most $2^{-1}$, take the first interval containing infinitely many values, and repeat inside it with successive meshes $2^{-2},2^{-3},\ldots$, always selecting the first subinterval with infinitely many retained indices. The nested intervals have diameters tending to zero, so the least increasing indices in the nested sets give a convergent subsequence. Use the enumeration fixed by [F5], and repeat this deterministic extraction successively on the current subsequence at each enumerated rational that lies in $[-R,R]$, skipping the others. The nested subsequences yield a diagonal subsequence converging at every rational point; each interval and index is selected by a least-index rule, so this uses no choice axiom. Given $\delta>0$, choose a finite rational partition of $[-R,R]$ with mesh at most $\delta$, possible by [F4]. For each subinterval $J=[r_i,r_{i+1}]$ and any two selected functions $v_p,v_q$, variation gives $|v_p(x)-v_q(x)|\le|v_p(r_i)-v_q(r_i)|+\operatorname{Var}_J(v_p)+\operatorname{Var}_J(v_q)$ for almost every $x\in J$. Integrating and summing yields $\|v_p-v_q\|_{L^1([-R,R])}\le 2\delta V+2R\max_i|v_p(r_i)-v_q(r_i)|.$ For the fixed partition the maximum tends to zero as $p,q\to\infty$; then taking $\delta\downarrow0$ proves the selected sections are Cauchy in local $L^1$. [F2, F4, F6, given, choose]

## Statement

Use the first-order HLL update of
[[def-pe03-first-order-hll-finite-volume-update]]. At a face with left and right
states $U_L,U_R$, supplied speeds $S_L<0<S_R$, and physical flux values
$F_L=F(U_L),F_R=F(U_R)$, define
$$U_*:=\frac{S_RU_R-S_LU_L-(F_R-F_L)}{S_R-S_L}.$$
If the one-sided CFL bounds $2\nu(-S_L)\le1$ and $2\nu S_R\le1$ hold, the
averages of the HLL fan over the adjacent left and right half-cells are,
respectively,
$$A^-=(1-2\nu(-S_L))U_L+2\nu(-S_L)U_*,\qquad A^+=(1-2\nu S_R)U_R+2\nu S_RU_*.$$
For every cell $i$, the updated mean satisfies
$$U_i^+=\frac12\left(A^+_{i-1/2}+A^-_{i+1/2}\right),$$
where each face uses its own supplied speeds and intermediate state.

## Definition

Let $K$ be a finite oriented three-dimensional cell complex with vertex, edge, face, and volume cochains. An edge cochain records oriented electric line integrals, a face cochain records oriented magnetic fluxes, and a vertex cochain records electric charge. Write $N_v,N_e,N_f,N_c$ for the retained vertex, edge, face, and cell counts. On a periodic cell, identify opposite cells with orientation preserved and let $G,C,D$ be the full vertex-to-edge gradient, edge-to-face curl, and face-to-cell divergence incidence matrices, each the transpose of its signed oriented boundary matrix. For a PEC closure, “interior” means not in the boundary subcomplex. Keep only interior electric edges as unknowns and only interior vertices as volume-charge locations, but keep all face fluxes, including boundary-normal magnetic fluxes, and all cells. This closure has no separate boundary surface-charge cochain. Define $G$ and $C$ by restricting the absolute vertex-edge and edge-face incidence matrices to those rows and columns. This mixed closure imposes zero tangential electric edge cochains on the boundary while allowing a fixed normal magnetic flux on boundary faces. In both cases, $G\in\mathbb R^{N_e\times N_v}$, $C\in\mathbb R^{N_f\times N_e}$, and $D\in\mathbb R^{N_c\times N_f}$ satisfy $CG=0$ and $DC=0$.

The electric, magnetic, and conductive material matrices are real symmetric matrices $M_e\in\mathbb R^{N_e\times N_e}$, $M_b\in\mathbb R^{N_f\times N_f}$, and $S\in\mathbb R^{N_e\times N_e}$, respectively. The first two are positive definite and represent the discrete weighted inner products induced by $\epsilon$ and $\mu^{-1}$; $S$ is positive semidefinite and represents conductivity. Write $\langle e_1,e_2\rangle_{M_e}=e_1^TM_ee_2$, $\langle b_1,b_2\rangle_{M_b}=b_1^TM_bb_2$, and $\|e\|_{M_e}^2=\langle e,e\rangle_{M_e}$, $\|b\|_{M_b}^2=\langle b,b\rangle_{M_b}$. In a homogeneous isotropic periodic Cartesian grid with spacings $h_x,h_y,h_z$ and cell volume $V=h_xh_yh_z$, the diagonal entries for an $x$-edge and an $x$-normal face are $\epsilon V/h_x^2=\epsilon h_yh_z/h_x$ and $\mu^{-1}h_x/(h_yh_z)$; the $y$ and $z$ entries are obtained by cyclic permutation. These values are dual-volume Hodge weights for line-integral and face-flux cochains. A compatible PEC closure uses the corresponding truncated dual volumes for free electric edges, while the magnetic mass includes boundary faces; the resulting matrices remain positive definite. The discrete constraints are $G^TM_ee^n=\rho^n$ on interior vertices and $Db^{n-1/2}=0$ on all cells.

For current cochains $j^{n+1/2}$ and charge rows $\rho^n$, the discrete continuity condition means
$$\rho^{n+1}-\rho^n+\Delta t\,G^T\left(j^{n+1/2}+S\frac{e^{n+1}+e^n}{2}\right)=0.$$
For PEC this is the interior-vertex volume-charge relation; this closure has no separate boundary surface-charge/current cochain.

The cochain identities $CG=0$ and $DC=0$ are not imposed as an extra numerical approximation: they follow from oriented boundary-of-boundary cancellation, including the PEC row and column restrictions, as proved in [[lem-maxwell-discrete-incidence-identities]]. No cell geometry picture is used as a proof.

## Definition

Let $K$ be a finite oriented three-dimensional cell complex with vertex, edge, face, and volume cochains. An edge cochain records oriented electric line integrals, a face cochain records oriented magnetic fluxes, and a vertex cochain records electric charge. Write $N_v,N_e,N_f,N_c$ for the retained vertex, edge, face, and cell counts. On a periodic cell, identify opposite cells with orientation preserved and let $G,C,D$ be the full vertex-to-edge gradient, edge-to-face curl, and face-to-cell divergence incidence matrices, each the transpose of its signed oriented boundary matrix. For a PEC closure, “interior” means not in the boundary subcomplex. Keep only interior electric edges as unknowns and only interior vertices as volume-charge locations, but keep all face fluxes, including boundary-normal magnetic fluxes, and all cells. This closure has no separate boundary surface-charge cochain. Define $G$ and $C$ by restricting the absolute vertex-edge and edge-face incidence matrices to those rows and columns. This mixed closure imposes zero tangential electric edge cochains on the boundary while allowing a fixed normal magnetic flux on boundary faces. In both cases, $G\in\mathbb R^{N_e\times N_v}$, $C\in\mathbb R^{N_f\times N_e}$, and $D\in\mathbb R^{N_c\times N_f}$ satisfy $CG=0$ and $DC=0$.

The electric, magnetic, and conductive material matrices are real symmetric matrices $M_e\in\mathbb R^{N_e\times N_e}$, $M_b\in\mathbb R^{N_f\times N_f}$, and $S\in\mathbb R^{N_e\times N_e}$, respectively. The first two are positive definite and represent the discrete weighted inner products induced by $\epsilon$ and $\mu^{-1}$; $S$ is positive semidefinite and represents conductivity. Write $\langle e_1,e_2\rangle_{M_e}=e_1^TM_ee_2$, $\langle b_1,b_2\rangle_{M_b}=b_1^TM_bb_2$, and $\|e\|_{M_e}^2=\langle e,e\rangle_{M_e}$, $\|b\|_{M_b}^2=\langle b,b\rangle_{M_b}$. In a homogeneous isotropic periodic Cartesian grid with spacings $h_x,h_y,h_z$ and cell volume $V=h_xh_yh_z$, the diagonal entries for an $x$-edge and an $x$-normal face are $\epsilon V/h_x^2=\epsilon h_yh_z/h_x$ and $\mu^{-1}h_x/(h_yh_z)$; the $y$ and $z$ entries are obtained by cyclic permutation. These values are dual-volume Hodge weights for line-integral and face-flux cochains. A compatible PEC closure uses the corresponding truncated dual volumes for free electric edges, while the magnetic mass includes boundary faces; the resulting matrices remain positive definite. The discrete constraints are $G^TM_ee^n=\rho^n$ on interior vertices and $Db^{n-1/2}=0$ on all cells.

For current cochains $j^{n+1/2}$ and charge rows $\rho^n$, the discrete continuity condition means
$$\rho^{n+1}-\rho^n+\Delta t\,G^T\left(j^{n+1/2}+S\frac{e^{n+1}+e^n}{2}\right)=0.$$
For PEC this is the interior-vertex volume-charge relation; this closure has no separate boundary surface-charge/current cochain.

The cochain identities $CG=0$ and $DC=0$ are not imposed as an extra numerical approximation: they follow from oriented boundary-of-boundary cancellation, including the PEC row and column restrictions, as proved in [[lem-maxwell-discrete-incidence-identities]]. ## Statement

Let $E:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be the actual exact-branch error map of one fixed
FAS two-grid or recursive V/W cycle, with $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ open. Let
$u_*\in U$ be a fine root for which the selected smoothers and coarse branches
fix $u_*$, so $E(u_*)=u_*$. Assume $E$ is $C^1$ on a neighborhood of the
closed Euclidean ball $K=\overline B_2(u_*,r)\subset U$. Put
$q=\|DE(u_*)\|_{\rm op}$, where for a linear map $T$ the induced Euclidean
operator norm is $\|T\|_{\rm op}:=\sup_{\|v\|_2=1}\|Tv\|_2$. Suppose $q<1$ and
$$\|DE(x)-DE(y)\|_{\rm op}\le L\|x-y\|_2\qquad(x,y\in K)$$
for some $L\ge0$. If $q+Lr/2<1$, then $E(K)\subseteq K$ and every iteration
$u_{k+1}=E(u_k)$ starting in $K$ satisfies
$$\|u_k-u_*\|_2\le(q+Lr/2)^k\|u_0-u_*\|_2.$$
This is a local result for the derivative of the actual cycle; it supplies no
global-start or mesh-independent rate unless $q,L,r$ are verified uniformly.

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the fixed nonempty bounded polyhedral domain, matching shape-regular affine simplicial mesh, and Nitsche face-height convention of [[def-nitsche-boundary-penalty-forms]]. Let $h:=\max_Kh_K$, $\ell_\Omega:=\operatorname{diam}(\Omega)$, and $1/2<s\le1$. For every $\zeta\in H^{1+s}(\Omega)$, with no boundary-value or PDE assumption,
$$\left(\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}h_F\|\partial_n\zeta\|_{L^2(F)}^2\right)^{1/2}\le C h^{1/2}\|\zeta\|_{H^{1+s}(\Omega)}=C_T h^{1/2}\ell_\Omega^{1/2}\|\zeta\|_{H^{1+s}(\Omega)},\qquad C_T:=C\ell_\Omega^{-1/2}.$$
The trace is the restriction of the whole-space Fourier hyperplane trace and agrees with the facet trace in [[lem-nitsche-fractional-face-trace-on-simplex]]. The constant $C_T$ may depend on the fixed domain, $d$, $s$, and the Fourier normalization, but not on the mesh.

## Statement

For $U\in\mathcal G$, let $Z=(Z_1,\ldots,Z_d)$ and $W=(W_1,\ldots,W_d)$ be arrays of entropy-variable gradients, with $Z_k,W_k\in\mathbb R^{d+2}$. Write $Z_{k,m_\ell}$ for the momentum-variable component and $Z_{k,E}$ for the energy-variable component. Define

$$G_{k\ell}(Z)=Z_{k,m_\ell}+u_\ell Z_{k,E},\qquad c_k(Z)=Z_{k,E},$$

and $G^0(Z)=\operatorname{sym}G(Z)-(\operatorname{tr}G(Z)/d)I$. Define the linear map

$$\mathcal R_U Z=\bigl(\sqrt{2\mu T}\,G^0(Z),\ \sqrt{\zeta T}\,\operatorname{tr}G(Z),\ \sqrt{\kappa}\,T c(Z)\bigr).$$

The bilinear form

$$\mathcal B_U(Z,W)=2\mu T\,G^0(Z):G^0(W)+\zeta T\,\operatorname{tr}G(Z)\operatorname{tr}G(W)+\kappa T^2\sum_{k=1}^d c_k(Z)c_k(W)$$

has the factorization $\mathcal B_U(Z,W)=(\mathcal R_UZ)\cdot(\mathcal R_UW)=\sum_{j,k}Z_j^TK_{jk}(U)W_k$, so $K(U)=\mathcal R_U^*\mathcal R_U$ is a symmetric positive-semidefinite block matrix. For $Z_k=\partial_kv(U)$, its blocks give exactly the model viscous flux $F_j^{\mathrm{visc}}=\sum_kK_{jk}(U)\partial_kv$, and

$$\sum_{j,k}(\partial_jv)^TK_{jk}(U)(\partial_kv)=\frac{\tau:\nabla u}{T}+\frac{\kappa|\nabla T|^2}{T^2}\ge0.$$

2.1 For a general array $Z$, define $\tau_{k\ell}(Z)=2\mu T G^0(Z)_{k\ell}+\zeta T\operatorname{tr}G(Z)\delta_{k\ell}$. The displayed bilinear form expands to $\mathcal B_U(Z,W)=\sum_{k,\ell}(W_{k,m_\ell}+u_\ell W_{k,E})\tau_{k\ell}(Z)+\kappa T^2\sum_kW_{k,E}Z_{k,E}$. Thus the linear functional in $W$ is pairing against the flux with zero mass row, momentum entries $\tau_{k\ell}(Z)$, and energy entry $u\cdot\tau_{k\cdot}(Z)+\kappa T^2Z_{k,E}$. By step 1.1 this is precisely the physical viscous flux when $Z=\nabla v$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The linear map $\mathcal R_U$ in the Statement gives $\mathcal B_U(Z,W)=(\mathcal R_UZ)\cdot(\mathcal R_UW)$ term by term. Its adjoint therefore defines the block matrix $K(U)=\mathcal R_U^*\mathcal R_U$, which is symmetric and positive semidefinite because $Z^TK(U)Z=|\mathcal R_UZ|^2\ge0$. In particular, for $W=Z$ the quadratic form equals $2\mu T|G^0(Z)|^2+\zeta T(\operatorname{tr}G(Z))^2+\kappa T^2\sum_k Z_{k,E}^2\ge0$, using $T>0$, $\mu>0$, $\zeta\ge0$, and $\kappa>0$. [F1, step 2.1, algebra]

## Definition

Let $u$ be upper semicontinuous and $v$ lower semicontinuous on the periodic
space-time cylinder. A **second-order parabolic viscosity subsolution** of
[[def-na-periodic-diagonal-controlled-diffusion-hjb-problem]] is a function $u$
such that every $C^{1,2}$ test function $\phi$ for which $u-\phi$ has a local
maximum at $(x_0,t_0)$, $0<t_0<T$, satisfies
$$\phi_t(x_0,t_0)-\max_{a\in A}\left\{\sum_j\left(\alpha_j^a\phi_{x_jx_j}+b_j^a\phi_{x_j}\right)(x_0,t_0)+f^a(x_0,t_0)\right\}\le0.$$
Here $C^{1,2}$ means that $\phi_t$, all first spatial derivatives, and all
second spatial derivatives exist and are continuous near the contact point.
A **supersolution** is lower semicontinuous and satisfies the reverse
inequality at every local minimum. A viscosity solution is both. For the Cauchy
problem, the relaxed initial conditions are
$$\limsup_{(y,s)\to(x,0),\ s>0}u(y,s)\le u_0(x),\qquad \liminf_{(y,s)\to(x,0),\ s>0}v(y,s)\ge u_0(x).$$

## Definition

Fix a dimension $d\ge1$, finite mode bounds $K_r\ge0$, a finite type-1 source list $(x_j,c_j)_{j<N}$ or type-2 data $(x_j)_{j<N},(f_k)_{k\in\mathcal K}$ as in [[def-nufft-transform-types-and-mode-conventions]], and a nonempty finite ordered list of candidate tuples
$$\mathcal C=\bigl((\tau_r,M_r,w_r,L_r)_{r=1}^d\bigr)_{\nu=1}^C,$$
an interval-arithmetic format $(p,e_{\min},e_{\max})$ with integers $p\ge2$ and $e_{\min}\le e_{\max}$, and one operationwise arithmetic model from [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]] with the same binary precision $p$ and normal exponent limits $j_{\min}=e_{\min}$ and $j_{\max}=e_{\max}$. Let $u$ be a valid unit-roundoff bound for this selected model instance; it is not a separate free control, and require $u\le1/16$. Use this same model instance for every computed FFT operation. Let $J\ge1$ be the finite elementary-series truncation index, $0\le\epsilon_{\rm tw}\le1/4$ an exact rational maximum allowed twiddle certificate, $0<\delta_{\phi}\le1/4$ an exact rational phase-evaluation tolerance, integers $2\le p_{\phi,0}\le p_{\phi,\max}$ giving the initial and maximum phase precisions, and a finite recursion-depth cap $d_{\rm FFT}\ge0$. The phase evaluator uses exponent limits $e_{\min},e_{\max}$ and truncation index $J$. Also supply an exact positive dyadic requested absolute tolerance $\varepsilon_{\rm req}>0$. Source coordinates and coefficients are finite dyadics interpreted as exact real and complex inputs. Each candidate must have rational $\tau_r>0$, a power-of-two grid length $M_r=2^{q_r}$ with integer $q_r\ge0$, $M_r>2K_r$, integer width $w_r\ge1$ with $M_r\ge2w_r+1$, and integer image cutoff $L_r\ge1$. A malformed global control or structurally invalid candidate returns `invalid-input` before arithmetic. Type 3 is not an input mode for this algorithm.

After validating the global controls and candidate shapes, if $N=0$ return status certified immediately: type 1 returns the exact zero output array and zero radii, and type 2 returns the empty output array and zero radius. For $N>0$, process the candidates in supplied order; the first candidate that produces a complete interval certificate meeting $\varepsilon_{\rm req}$ is returned.

1. For each coordinate compute outward enclosures for
$$a_r=\frac{\pi}{\tau_rM_r^2},\quad s_r=\exp\!\bigl(-\pi\tau_rM_r(M_r-2K_r)\bigr),\quad d_r=\sqrt{\tau_r}\exp(-\pi\tau_rK_r^2),$$
$$S_r=\frac2{1-\exp(-a_r)},\quad T_r=2\exp(-a_rw_r^2)\left(1+\frac{1}{2a_rw_r}\right),\quad R_r=\frac{2\exp(-\pi L_r^2/\tau_r)}{1-\exp(-\pi L_r/\tau_r)}.$$
Use [[alg-certified-elementary-range-evaluation]] for every real exponential and square-root node in the procedure, including the finite norms, normalization and complex moduli; use format $(p,e_{\min},e_{\max})$ and truncation index $N=J$ on every such call. Form every Machin enclosure of $\pi$ with this same format and index. Use the outward interval operations for the rational DAGs. Set
$$A=\prod_{r=1}^d\left(1+\frac{2s_r}{1-s_r}\right)-1,\qquad T_d=\sum_{r=1}^dT_r\prod_{s\ne r}S_s,\qquad d_{\min}=\prod_{r=1}^d d_r.$$
Store outward upper bounds $A^+,T_d^+$ and $R_r^+$, where $R_r^+$ bounds the exact image-tail constant $R_r$, and a lower bound $d_{\min}^-$. If any required enclosure is non-finite, if a required denominator interval in $A,S_r,T_r,R_r$ contains zero, if some $s_r$ enclosure is not strictly below $1$, or if $d_{\min}^-\le0$, reject this candidate as inconclusive; no division by an unverified multiplier is performed.

2. For every source define its periodic nearest-point set by
$$W_j=\prod_{r=1}^d\left\{\ell_r\in\{0,\ldots,M_r-1\}: \min_{n\in\mathbb Z}|\ell_r/M_r-x_{j,r}-n|\le w_r/M_r\right\},$$
using the selected candidate. For type 1 only, for each $\ell\in W_j$ reduce each exact dyadic displacement $\ell_r/M_r-x_{j,r}$ modulo one to $z_r\in[0,1)$. Enclose the one-dimensional kernel by evaluating the finite image sum
$$\sum_{n=-L_r}^{L_r}\exp\!\left(-\pi(z_r+n)^2/\tau_r\right)$$
with [[alg-certified-elementary-range-evaluation]] using $N=J$, then add the symmetric interval $[-R_r^+,R_r^+]$ from step 1. All kernel and coefficient products and sums use outward interval arithmetic. For each grid cell $\ell$, this gives a complex rectangle enclosing its exact truncated-spread value $g_\ell$. Choose its lower-left corner $u_\ell$ as a dyadic center and an upward dyadic radius $e_\ell$ large enough to enclose $g_\ell-u_\ell$. Let $E_{\rm eval}$ be an outward upper bound for $(\sum_\ell e_\ell^2)^{1/2}$ and let $U$ be an outward upper bound for $\|u\|_2=(\sum_\ell|u_\ell|^2)^{1/2}$. Before a type-1 FFT call, require every real and imaginary coordinate of every $u_\ell$ to belong to the representable set $\mathbb F$ of the selected operationwise model; otherwise reject this candidate with a range-failure status before calling the FFT. Type 2 skips this spreading-grid construction; its source-window intervals are evaluated in step 4 using the sets $W_j$ just defined.

3. For each mode $k\in\mathcal K$, define its grid slot by $\kappa(k)=(k_r\bmod M_r)_{r=1}^d$, using least nonnegative residues; $M_r>2K_r$ makes this map injective. Put $\eta=10u+\epsilon_{\rm tw}$, $\rho_r=(1+\eta)^{q_r}-1$ for each axis, and $\rho=\prod_r(1+\rho_r)-1$. For type 1, run [[alg-na-computed-unitary-radix-two-fft]] on each length-$M_r$ grid line along axes $1,\ldots,d$ in a fixed lexicographic line order, with direction `forward`, the selected operationwise model, phase tolerance $\delta_{\phi}$, exponent limits $e_{\min},e_{\max}$, phase precisions $p_{\phi,0},p_{\phi,\max}$, series cap $J$, and recursion cap $d_{\rm FFT}$. The supplier passes the exact rational phase argument $q=-2m/M_r$ for its twiddle indexed by $m$ and returns a certificate $\epsilon_\ell$ for each twiddle it uses. Reject this candidate with the returned status if an FFT call is non-finite or inconclusive; otherwise verify for every returned twiddle certificate that $\epsilon_\ell\le\epsilon_{\rm tw}$. If any certificate exceeds $\epsilon_{\rm tw}$, reject this candidate with status `twiddle-bound-not-met` and do not use that FFT output. This check applies literally when $\epsilon_{\rm tw}=0$, so every used twiddle must then have certificate zero. After all checks pass, extract the unitary Fourier coordinates at slots $\kappa(k)$ for $k\in\mathcal K$ and scale by $P^{-1/2}$, where $P=\prod_rM_r$. Use the range evaluator with format $(p,e_{\min},e_{\max})$ and $N=J$ for every real elementary node, including this scaling and the mode multipliers; use the same $J$ Machin enclosure of $\pi$. For each required mode evaluate the multiplier interval $d_k=\prod_r\sqrt{\tau_r}\exp(-\pi\tau_rk_r^2)$; if its lower endpoint is $\le0$, reject this candidate as inconclusive before division. Otherwise divide by that certified positive interval. Use outward complex-rectangle arithmetic. For each $k\in\mathcal K$, choose the lower-left corner $z_k$ of this computed scaling/deconvolution rectangle and an upward dyadic radius $b_k$ containing that rectangle about $z_k$. This rectangle alone concerns the computed FFT output, not the exact unitary transform. Separately form a certified outward upper bound $R_{\rm FFT}$ for
$$\frac{\rho U}{\sqrt P\,d_{\min}^-}.$$
Here $U$ is the certified norm bound of the actual dyadic input grid from step 2, and $\rho$ uses the same selected model's valid bound $u$ and checked twiddle limit $\epsilon_{\rm tw}$ as the successful FFT calls. Evaluate this nonnegative radius DAG with outward interval operations: integer powers use finite products, and the normalization square root uses the same range format and index $J$. As with the existing model and rational constants, use certified enclosing constants throughout; in particular enclose the selected model's valid unit-roundoff bound. If that model supplies no tighter certified enclosure for $u$, use the already verified enclosure $[0,1/16]$, converted outward to the selected format; thus no additional oracle or input for $u$ is required. Reject the candidate as inconclusive if any radius enclosure is non-finite or the normalization denominator enclosure is not strictly positive before division. Define the returned coordinate radius by the upward dyadic sum $r_k=\operatorname{ru}(b_k+R_{\rm FFT})$; if this sum overflows, reject the candidate with its range status. Thus every returned radius includes both the scaling/deconvolution rectangle and the separately bounded error of its computed FFT relative to the exact transform of the dyadic center grid. Set
$$\epsilon_{\rm ana}=A^++\frac{T_d^+}{P\,d_{\min}^-},\qquad B_{\rm round}=\max_{k\in\mathcal K}r_k+ \frac{E_{\rm eval}}{\sqrt{P}\,d_{\min}^-}.$$
The returned error certificate is $\epsilon_{\rm ana}$ and $B_{\rm round}$.

The phase evaluator uses exponent limits $e_{\min},e_{\max}$ and truncation index $J$. Also supply an exact positive dyadic requested absolute tolerance $\varepsilon_{\rm req}>0$. Source coordinates and coefficients are finite dyadics interpreted as exact real and complex inputs. Each candidate must have rational $\tau_r>0$, a power-of-two grid length $M_r=2^{q_r}$ with integer $q_r\ge0$, $M_r>2K_r$, integer width $w_r\ge1$ with $M_r\ge2w_r+1$, and integer image cutoff $L_r\ge1$. After validating the global controls and candidate shapes, if $N=0$ return status certified immediately: type 1 returns the exact zero output array and zero radii, and type 2 returns the empty output array and zero radius. 1. For each coordinate compute outward enclosures for

Form every Machin enclosure of $\pi$ with this same format and index. Use the outward interval operations for the rational DAGs. Set
$$A=\prod_{r=1}^d\left(1+\frac{2s_r}{1-s_r}\right)-1,\qquad T_d=\sum_{r=1}^dT_r\prod_{s\ne r}S_s,\qquad d_{\min}=\prod_{r=1}^d d_r.$$
Store outward upper bounds $A^+,T_d^+$ and $R_r^+$, where $R_r^+$ bounds the exact image-tail constant $R_r$, and a lower bound $d_{\min}^-$. $$W_j=\prod_{r=1}^d\left\{\ell_r\in\{0,\ldots,M_r-1\}: \min_{n\in\mathbb Z}|\ell_r/M_r-x_{j,r}-n|\le w_r/M_r\right\},$$

$$\sum_{n=-L_r}^{L_r}\exp\!\left(-\pi(z_r+n)^2/\tau_r\right)$$

Choose its lower-left corner $u_\ell$ as a dyadic center and an upward dyadic radius $e_\ell$ large enough to enclose $g_\ell-u_\ell$. This rectangle alone concerns the computed FFT output, not the exact unitary transform. Separately form a certified outward upper bound $R_{\rm FFT}$ for
$$\frac{\rho U}{\sqrt P\,d_{\min}^-}.$$
Here $U$ is the certified norm bound of the actual dyadic input grid from step 2, and $\rho$ uses the same selected model's valid bound $u$ and checked twiddle limit $\epsilon_{\rm tw}$ as the successful FFT calls. Evaluate this nonnegative radius DAG with outward interval operations: integer powers use finite products, and the normalization square root uses the same range format and index $J$. As with the existing model and rational constants, use certified enclosing constants throughout; in particular enclose the selected model's valid unit-roundoff bound. If that model supplies no tighter certified enclosure for $u$, use the already verified enclosure $[0,1/16]$, converted outward to the selected format; thus no additional oracle or input for $u$ is required. Define the returned coordinate radius by the upward dyadic sum $r_k=\operatorname{ru}(b_k+R_{\rm FFT})$; if this sum overflows, reject the candidate with its range status. $$\epsilon_{\rm ana}=A^++\frac{T_d^+}{P\,d_{\min}^-},\qquad B_{\rm round}=\max_{k\in\mathcal K}r_k+ \frac{E_{\rm eval}}{\sqrt{P}\,d_{\min}^-}.$$
The returned error certificate is $\epsilon_{\rm ana}$ and $B_{\rm round}$.

For each input mode $k$, evaluate its multiplier interval using the same format and truncation setting $N=J$; if its lower endpoint is $\le0$, reject the candidate as inconclusive before division. Otherwise divide by that certified positive interval. For the resulting mode rectangles choose lower-left dyadic centers $v_k$ and radii $e_k$ enclosing their deviations. Set $E_f$ to an outward upper bound for $(\sum_ke_k^2)^{1/2}$ and $V$ to an outward upper bound for $\|v\|_2$. Require every real and imaginary coordinate of the $v_k$ to belong to $\mathbb F$; otherwise reject this candidate with a range-failure status before calling the FFT. Embed each $v_k$ at grid slot $\kappa(k)$, zero-fill all unused grid modes with zero centers and zero radii, and apply [[alg-na-computed-unitary-radix-two-fft]] in direction `inverse` on the same axes and in the same lexicographic line order, passing the same operationwise model and phase controls as in type 1. Enlarge the unitary-grid output by radius $E_f+\rho V$ and scale by $P^{-1/2}$. Multiply the coordinate window intervals, conjugate the resulting real window (which leaves it unchanged), and multiply and sum against the scaled grid rectangles using outward complex-rectangle arithmetic at every operation. ## Statement

Let $a<b$, $f\in C^4[a,b]$ be complex-valued, and $g\in C^7[a,b]$ be real-valued. Suppose $g'(x_0)=0$, $g''(x_0)\ne0$ for one $x_0\in(a,b)$, and $g'$ has no other zero on $[a,b]$. Choose a coordinate $\Phi:J\to(-R,R)$ from [[lem-na-one-dimensional-morse-coordinate]], after restricting its domain, and an even $\eta\in C_c^\infty((-R,R))$ equal to $1$ near $0$. Such a cutoff exists by symmetrizing a bump from [[lem-euclidean-bump-for-a-compact-set-inside-an-open-set]]. Extend $\chi(x)=\eta(\Phi(x))$ by $0$ outside $J$, put $h=(1-\chi)f$, $A(u)=\eta(u)f(\Phi^{-1}(u))(\Phi^{-1})'(u)$, and $\sigma=\operatorname{sgn}(\omega g''(x_0))$. For $|\omega|\ge1$,
$$I_\omega(f,g;[a,b])=\frac{1}{i\omega}\left[\frac{f(x)e^{i\omega g(x)}}{g'(x)}\right]_a^b+f(x_0)e^{i\omega g(x_0)}\sqrt{\frac{2\pi}{|\omega g''(x_0)|}}e^{i\sigma\pi/4}+\mathcal R_\omega,$$
where
$$|\mathcal R_\omega|\le\left(C_{R,\eta}\|A\|_{C^4}+|T_gh(a)/g'(a)|+|T_gh(b)/g'(b)|+(b-a)\|T_g^2h\|_\infty\right)|\omega|^{-3/2}.$$
On the neighborhood where $h=0$, define $T_gh$ and $T_g^2h$ to be $0$; elsewhere use the recurrence from [[def-na-finite-interval-oscillatory-integral]]. The nonstationary norm is taken over the two closed intervals away from that neighborhood.

## Statement

Let $a<b$, $f\in C^4[a,b]$ be complex-valued, and $g\in C^7[a,b]$ be real-valued. Suppose $g'(x_0)=0$, $g''(x_0)\ne0$ for one $x_0\in(a,b)$, and $g'$ has no other zero on $[a,b]$. Choose a coordinate $\Phi:J\to(-R,R)$ from [[lem-na-one-dimensional-morse-coordinate]], after restricting its domain, and an even $\eta\in C_c^\infty((-R,R))$ equal to $1$ near $0$. Such a cutoff exists by symmetrizing a bump from [[lem-euclidean-bump-for-a-compact-set-inside-an-open-set]]. Extend $\chi(x)=\eta(\Phi(x))$ by $0$ outside $J$, put $h=(1-\chi)f$, $A(u)=\eta(u)f(\Phi^{-1}(u))(\Phi^{-1})'(u)$, and $\sigma=\operatorname{sgn}(\omega g''(x_0))$. For $|\omega|\ge1$,
$$I_\omega(f,g;[a,b])=\frac{1}{i\omega}\left[\frac{f(x)e^{i\omega g(x)}}{g'(x)}\right]_a^b+f(x_0)e^{i\omega g(x_0)}\sqrt{\frac{2\pi}{|\omega g''(x_0)|}}e^{i\sigma\pi/4}+\mathcal R_\omega,$$
where
$$|\mathcal R_\omega|\le\left(C_{R,\eta}\|A\|_{C^4}+|T_gh(a)/g'(a)|+|T_gh(b)/g'(b)|+(b-a)\|T_g^2h\|_\infty\right)|\omega|^{-3/2}.$$
On the neighborhood where $h=0$, define $T_gh$ and $T_g^2h$ to be $0$; elsewhere use the recurrence from [[def-na-finite-interval-oscillatory-integral]]. The nonstationary norm is taken over the two closed intervals away from that neighborhood.

## Definition

Fix a local characteristic family on a neighborhood where it is either
genuinely nonlinear with constant sign $d_i=D\lambda_i\,r_i\ne0$, or linearly
degenerate. For a genuinely nonlinear family define
$$\Psi_i(\sigma;u)=\begin{cases}R_i(\sigma;u),&\sigma d_i>0,\\S_i(\sigma;u),&\sigma d_i<0,\\u,&\sigma=0.\end{cases}$$
where $R_i$ is the local rarefaction curve and $S_i$ the local shock curve of
[[lem-local-characteristic-shock-curve]]. For a linearly degenerate family set
$\Psi_i(\sigma;u)=R_i(\sigma;u)$ for either sign; its nonzero-strength wave is
the contact of [[lem-linearly-degenerate-characteristic-contact]]. The
parameter $\sigma$ is local and is restricted so the entire curve stays in the
chosen neighborhood.

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega^-,\Gamma,\Omega^+$ have the $C^2$ geometry of [[def-bem-smooth-helmholtz-combined-field-operator]]. If $u\in H^1(\Omega^+\cap B_R)$ for every ball containing $\overline{\Omega^-}$ solves $(\Delta+k^2)u=0$ weakly for a real $k>0$, has zero trace on $\Gamma$, and satisfies
$$\lim_{r\to\infty}\sup_{\omega\in\mathbb S^2}|r(\partial_r-ik)u(r\omega)|=0,$$
then $u=0$ on $\Omega^+$. The radiation condition refers to the smooth representative away from the boundary.

2.1 Choose $a$ so large that $\overline{\Omega^-}\subset B_a$, and fix $r>a$. The annular domain $B_r\setminus\overline{\Omega^-}$ has inner boundary $\Gamma$ and outer sphere. Its weak Green formula [F1], tested with $u$, gives $\int_{B_r\setminus\overline{\Omega^-}}(|\nabla u|^2-k^2|u|^2)dx=\int_{|x|=r}\partial_ru\bar u\,dS-\langle q^+,\gamma^+u\rangle.$ The last term is zero by the zero trace. The left side is real, hence $J(r)=r^2\operatorname{Im}\int_{\mathbb S^2}\partial_ru(r\omega)\overline{u(r\omega)}d\omega=0$. Only the original obstacle boundary has zero trace; no zero trace is assumed on the enclosing sphere. [F1, step 1.1, given, algebra]

3.1 At this fixed $r$, both $u(r,\cdot)$ and $\partial_ru(r,\cdot)$ are smooth, so their ordered harmonic projections converge in $L^2$ by [F2]. Cauchy–Schwarz passes the inner product to the limit of finite orthogonal sums. By [F2]–[F3], this gives $J(r)=\lim_{N\to\infty}\sum_{\ell=0}^N\|c_\ell\|_2^2/k.$ Every summand is nonnegative and step 2.1 gives zero, so all $c_\ell=0$. Completeness in [F2] now makes $u(r,\cdot)=0$ in $L^2$, hence pointwise by smoothness. This holds for every $r>a$, so $u=0$ on $|x|>a$. No degree sum was interchanged with the radiation limit at infinity. [F2, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

Let $\mathcal H_k(\mathbb R^d)$ consist of the inverse Fourier representatives $U_g$ with $\int |g(\xi)|^2/w(\xi)\,d\xi<\infty$, with inner product

Since $w>0$, the sum is zero almost everywhere. A continuous function zero almost everywhere is zero everywhere, because any point of nonzero value would have a neighborhood on which its modulus is bounded below, and such a neighborhood contains a positive-measure box [F5]. [F1, F5, F6, algebra]

4.1 Choose $v=(1,t,\ldots,t^{d-1})$ so that the numbers $v\cdot x_j$ are pairwise distinct. For each pair $i
e j$, the polynomial $(x_i-x_j)\cdot(1,t,\ldots,t^{d-1})$ is nonzero because $x_i-x_j
e0$; [F4] says its zero set is finite. The ordered field $\mathbb R$ has $0<1$, so the natural multiples $0,1,1+1,\ldots$ are strictly increasing and $\mathbb R$ is infinite. e j} rac{t-v\cdot x_i}{v\cdot x_j-v\cdot x_i}$$ has degree at most $N-1$ and satisfies $L_j(v\cdot x_i)=1$ if $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise. Taking the same linear combination of the moment equations as the coefficients of $L_j$ yields $c_j=0$. Thus all $c_j=0$, and the real Gram matrix is strictly positive definite. ## Definition

Choose a finite complex and boundary closure as in [[def-maxwell-discrete-cochain-and-yee-grid]], step size $\Delta t>0$, initial $e^0\in\mathbb R^{N_e}$ and $b^{-1/2}\in\mathbb R^{N_f}$, and source rows $j^{n+1/2}\in\mathbb R^{N_e}$. The output is a sequence $e^n$ at integer times and $b^{n+1/2}$ at half-integer times. For each $n\ge0$, perform the ordered instructions

1. Update the face flux by
   $$b^{n+1/2}=b^{n-1/2}-\Delta t\,C e^n.$$

2. Solve the electric row
   $$\left(M_e+\frac{\Delta t}{2}S\right)e^{n+1}=\left(M_e-\frac{\Delta t}{2}S\right)e^n+\Delta t\,C^TM_b b^{n+1/2}-\Delta t\,j^{n+1/2}.$$

For $S=0$ this is the lossless Yee leapfrog scheme. For $S\succeq0$, the midpoint term is the specified trapezoidal treatment of conductivity. The row is well defined for every input because its matrix is invertible by [[lem-maxwell-yee-step-matrix-is-positive-definite]]. This procedure makes no stability claim; the lossless stability condition is proved separately.

## Example

On the smooth spherical shell
$\Omega=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:1<|x|<2\}$, the field
$$u(x)=\frac{x}{|x|^3}$$
is nonzero, divergence-free and curl-free, and it satisfies the PEC closure
condition. It is orthogonal to every zero-boundary gradient, but it is not
the gradient of any $H_0^1(\Omega)$ potential. Thus a gauge that removes only
zero-boundary gradients leaves this topological zero mode; the full-kernel
quotient of [[def-na-pe11-maxwell-cavity-eigenproblem]] removes it.
